speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are suffering from severe abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and painful urination. To help you, I need to know more about your symptoms: how many hours has the pain been present, and does it radiate to your back or groin? Have you noticed any blood in your urine or fever?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old female. The patient presents with a 5-day history of severe abdominal pain and cramping, accompanied by nausea and vomiting. She reports pain with urination and also experienced burning pain during sexual intercourse 3 days ago. She mentions being sexually active with one male partner, using condoms inconsistently.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID) with secondary cystitis.

The history of dyspareunia, fever (if present), nausea, and vomiting in a sexually active 17-year-old strongly suggests an ascending infection like PID. I am requesting a urine analysis and a pelvic ultrasound to confirm the diagnosis and rule out other causes.

REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Urine Culture
REQUEST TEST: Pelvic_Ultrasound
REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvic_Imaging
